title: Is this a game you would actually play?
author: BeltwayBro
selftext:
I have built a handful of browser games over the last few months and this is the newest one in my "portfolio".  I'm really enjoying building it. I've learned how to rig 2D models and even have a cool workflow that allows me to have Claude take the first pass at rigging the animation, but then give me the ability to fine-tune things further at the frame level (granted I have not done a ton of tuning yet)

Anyhow, I've spent a bout 3 weeks on this (mostly nights and weekends). I like playing it but I wonder if this has real commercial legs? Is it too dark and gory for most folks?

So my honest question -- is this something you would play? Curious if I should keep investing some time in this one.

Here is the website I just put together as well. Pretty happy with how the more interactive elements turned out

[https://pivothouse.io/crimsonmarch](https://pivothouse.io/crimsonmarch)  
  
Beta is playable on mobile or desktop with no download needed:

And if you want to try out the beta, just use the access code "AIGAMEDEV". This will also give you some free epic gear to help with early progression.

comments.body:
Does anyone actually play browser games?

As to answer your question. Nope. Looks simplistic and I don't think I'd get any enjoyment out of it

replies.author: imlo2
replies.body: People have played browser games in the past and most likely will continue to do so. Not everyone has a fancy gaming PC or a console. Anyway, for example, millions of people have played games on Newgrounds and similar sites, and many of those Flash/JavaScript etc. games were pretty clunky.

replies.author: BeltwayBro
replies.body: Cool cool, yeah. Maybe "commercial legs" was the wrong framing here. Would just do otpional ads for monetization or something. Just tryign to determine if I should spend the $15 to get this published in google palystore and spend a few weeks polishing it up and adding more content

replies.author: FailedGradAdmissions
replies.body: Yeah, that's the only viable business model. When SilkSong is $20 and Undertale $10 if you launch a way less polished game even if you charge $5 nobody will buy it.  So if you want to recoup your time, it's either ads or microtransactions.

comments.author: iliadz
comments.body: The biggest part for me is I don't see the enemies attacking you. It seems from the trailer, it's a bit of you just killing them, and gaining points. Without there being a challenge I would not. That being said, it does look pretty good overall.

replies.author: BeltwayBro
replies.body: Thanks for responding here. Yeah they definitely attack and kill you. I still need to do some difficulty tuning. I think it's currently too hard to progress and maybe a little too grindy but I could be wrong.

comments.author: Briskfall
comments.body:
I would not play this. But imho it's more of a "i played something like this on my slow ass PC when I was 8-9 and it was like baby's first fantasy rpg" -- Current adult me can see all sorts of "issues" with it that younger me wouldn't. It's more like... I've outgrown the genre?...

It feels very slow tempo-wise, maybe okay for kids but even so I wouldn't choose this as a kid because it's way too dark for young me.

It's in this awkward spot where it looks "okay-ish" for something created in the 2002-2006, but I'm not sure as for the current "era"? It reminds me of old school flash animation way too much.

I wouldn't play it because the mechanisms are too "legacy" -- due to lacking fluidity, animation wind up taking too long, and it feels like menu scrolling takes much more time vs "giving me agency."

One good thing about it is that the art direction seems cohesive enough. Right now it's at best a "promo game" for a fast food restaurant chain where people "would play" to see how whack it would be.
